title: Six windows
summary: A wall with six windows, of which two are real. Photographed straight on, because it deserved to be.

body.text: Four of the six are blind: built as openings, bricked flush at some later date, and then — this is the part worth the photograph — painted to look like windows, including the glazing bars and a suggestion of reflection.

Somebody was paid to do that. Somebody stood on a ladder in the north of England and painted a picture of a window onto a wall, at a height where it would only ever be seen from an angle, and did a competent job of it.
The paint is failing on two of them and the brick is coming through, which means there is now a window painted onto a wall in the process of turning back into a wall.
